builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs
summary: Cleave replaces fine-tuning-based jailbreaks with training-free edits to residual writing weights that strip safety guardrails from open-weight LLMs, and its dual-stage defense replaces behavioral spot-checks with pre-release subspace diagnostics plus post-release weight-coupling audits. For a deployer it costs nothing to be aware of, but applying the defense requires access to the release pipeline and clean reference weights, and the selective-attack variant preserves 99% refusal on unrelated categories, so it can pass casual checks. What can fail after adoption: the audits may miss novel editing subspaces, and any safety posture that assumes downloaded weights retain their guardrails is unsound, so runtime input/output filtering remains necessary.
rationale: The reader deploys rather than releases open-weight models, so the actionable lesson is that embedded guardrails are trivially removable by weight editing and cannot be relied upon as a safety boundary, while the defense audits target model providers and are outside the reader's production scope.
technique: Training-free weight editing to remove LLM guardrails

claims.statement: Cleave replaces fine-tuning-based jailbreaks with training-free edits to residual writing weights that strip safety guardrails from open-weight LLMs, and its dual-stage defense replaces behavioral spot-checks with pre-release subspace diagnostics plus post-release weight-coupling audits. For a deployer it costs nothing to be aware of, but applying the defense requires access to the release pipeline and clean reference weights, and the selective-attack variant preserves 99% refusal on unrelated categories, so it can pass casual checks. What can fail after adoption: the audits may miss novel editing subspaces, and any safety posture that assumes downloaded weights retain their guardrails is unsound, so runtime input/output filtering remains necessary.
Attack achieves up to 67.97% success on seven safety benchmarks and up to 24x more executable exploits; the proposed defense reports 100% detection recall at 1% false-positive rate.
